version.author: Dead Pixel Design
version.changelog: The bridge script CHANGED this time - ReaPack users get new commands, not just a version number. REAPER has a preference, Preferences > Audio > "set media items offline when application is not active", that unloads disk media whenever REAPER is not the active application. It exists to save RAM and for normal hand-driven use it is invisible. It is not invisible to a daemon: every command arrives from another process (the CLI, the MCP server, the console sidecar), so REAPER is ALWAYS in the background when it runs one. With that preference on, every read saw unloaded media and a capture could measure sources that were not loaded. Virtual instruments were unaffected, having no file to unload, which is what made the symptom look like a plugin bug rather than a preference. It is now visible and fixable. get_context reports media_offline_when_inactive, and each FX entry carries offline and bypassed (authoritative reads). get_items reports a per-item source_state: loaded, offline (REAPER is not loading a file that is right there), unresolved (the file genuinely cannot be read - a different problem with a different fix), or midi. That state is INFERRED and ships with source_state_inferred: true, because REAPER exposes no ReaScript call for media-item offline state; it is derived from a source reporting zero length and zero sample rate while its file still opens from inside REAPER's process. get_capture_preflight warns when the preference is on, so a measurement never quietly reports a number taken against unloaded media. Two new commands: set_media_offline_when_inactive turns the preference off (gated at allow_risk_level_3, needs SWS, and always reads the value back rather than trusting the write), and set_all_media_online clears media that is already stranded - the state is sticky, and does not clear from restoring or focusing the window, from starting playback, or from turning the preference back off. This release also root-causes a long-standing trap in this repo's own notes, "a minimized REAPER window renders digital silence": minimizing was never the trigger, losing active-app status was, and the same preference explains why virtual instruments kept rendering while disk media went silent. All of it live-verified against a running REAPER on a real 24-track session, not offline-tested only.

version.author: Dead Pixel Design
version.changelog: The bridge script is unchanged; the version moves in lockstep with the repo release. Everything new lives in the cloned repo (ReaPack installs only this bridge; clone https://github.com/wretcher207/reaper-daemon for the CLI and the engines). The part-writing path is now on MCP: three new tools bring the total to 29. `insert_riff` renders ONE humanized guitar or bass part from inline riff text (or a riff file, or the built-in demo) and inserts it on a named track; `cut_band` lays down or re-cuts the whole four-track jam in one call (two double-tracked guitars on different seeds, a bass locked to them, drums from a DSL), attempting every leg even when an earlier one fails and reporting each leg separately; `humanize_take` puts a dynamic contour and micro-timing into a drum take already on a track, golden rule enforced, `follow_lead` included. All three share one write path with the CLI's `shred`, `band`, and `humanize`, so behavior does not differ by surface, and all three support `dry_run`. Fixed on the way: `insert_groove`'s private copy of that path deleted the rendered .mid after insert, which left an empty take on REAPER builds that hold MIDI by reference; rendered files now persist under rendered-midi/. All three tools live-verified against a running REAPER. Also new in the repo: the Daemon Console — a ReaImGui chat panel docked inside REAPER backed by a headless Claude Code session — is now fully documented in docs/CONSOLE.md (architecture, file protocol, trust statement, cost and liveness rules). The console is clone-only and deliberately does not ship through ReaPack: ReaPack delivers Lua only, and the panel is useless without its Python sidecar.

version.author: Dead Pixel Design
version.changelog: Playing release. The bridge script is unchanged; the version moves in lockstep with the repo release. Everything new lives in the cloned repo (ReaPack installs only this bridge; clone https://github.com/wretcher207/reaper-daemon for the CLI and the engines). Guitar: riffs connect instead of stabbing. Two new connection cells write phrases rather than a row of equal 16ths, `_` ties the previous note through this step (held over the barline) and `~` slides into the next one (firing Argent's Slide keyswitch); palm-muted chugs now carry up to two 16ths under the palm instead of being cut short, which is the body that makes one chug lead into the next; and a ringing note is held past the next attack so Shreddage slurs (hammer-on/pull-off) rather than re-picking, with anything not meant to slur clamped clear of the next onset so micro-timing can never leave a flam. Harmony: uppercase note names (E F G A B C D) are chord cells read in the key of E, each firing Power Chord Sustain so a section actually moves instead of pedaling the open string; lead scale tones fill the single-note gaps for melodies over those chords; and the bass reads a chord token as harmony and follows it rather than hammering the root. Case matters, uppercase is the chord and lowercase is a single note. Drums: kicks are floored across the board, and double-bass runs are pinned to a 105-112 velocity band with left-foot fatigue under the right. The no-repeat golden rule (no drum hits the same velocity twice in a row, per drum in time order, whatever lands between) is now hardline in a shared `drumgen/goldenrule.py` that every write path calls, with `enforce()` to apply it and `violations()` to prove it before a write. New flag: `reaperd.py humanize --follow-lead` learns the velocity hand out of the bars you humanized by hand and carries it across the rest of the take instead of applying the shared taste model, auto-detecting the first flat bar or taking `--example-through-bar`. Docs: the README now documents `shred`, `band`, and `humanize`, including the riff notation and the tuning maps.

version.author: Dead Pixel Design
version.changelog: Shreddage release. The bridge script is unchanged; the version moves in lockstep with the repo release. Everything new lives in the cloned repo (ReaPack installs only this bridge; clone https://github.com/wretcher207/reaper-daemon for the CLI and the engines): a guitar and bass MIDI apparatus that writes believable, human-feeling parts straight onto REAPER tracks. It ships tuning and keyswitch maps for Shreddage 3.5 Argent (9-string) and the GGD Nolly bass, a compact riff notation, and a performance engine that shares the drum humanizer's taste model (a musical contour drives the dynamics, randomness is only garnish, and a no-repeat rule keeps consecutive chugs off one velocity). Articulation is set by keyswitch: fast chugs palm mute, root accents and holds voice power chords, and dissonant palm-muted clusters ring over the low pedal. Double tracking is two real performances, not a stereo copy, so the two guitar takes get their width from different seeds. New CLI: `reaperd.py band` lays down or re-cuts a whole four-track jam (two guitars, bass, drums) in one command, replacing what was there; `shred` and `groove` gained a `--replace` flag; and guitar riff bars now allow spaces for readability. Also fixed: this REAPER build imports MIDI by reference, so the CLI keeps its rendered .mid files instead of deleting them (a deleted file left an empty take).

version.author: Dead Pixel Design
version.changelog: Maintenance. The undocumented enum_installed_fx command is removed (never in the schema, untested, uncalled, and duplicated by the CLI's installed-plugin resolver); no documented command changed. Repo-side (clone only, not ReaPack): the unreachable site/ product page is deleted (netlify.toml 301s everything to deadpixeldesign.com; the old page lives in git history), one-time console-spike tooling and a self-consistency fixture test are removed, and the drumgen.profile argv builder is shared between the CLI and the MCP server so the two cannot drift.

version.author: Dead Pixel Design
version.changelog: Daemon Beater release. The bridge script itself is unchanged; the version moves in lockstep with the repo release. Everything new lives in the cloned repo (ReaPack installs only this bridge; clone https://github.com/wretcher207/reaper-daemon for the CLI and the drum engine): `reaperd.py profile` reads a guitar stem bar by bar (onset density, timing regularity, palm-mute vs ringing decay, silence, band balance, a 16th-note accent grid, plus suggested section boundaries and repeat groups). Point it at any bar with --start-bar/--bars/--max-seconds and it analyzes just that window, never the whole stem, with hop-aligned cuts so timing, onset, grid, decay, and band numbers from a window match a full pass (only the silence ratio is scored against a window-local loudness reference). The palm-mute vs open decay read now survives real tempos (a fixed tail window used to swallow the next hit's attack once notes came faster than ~220ms apart), and the analysis passes run about 2x faster. The verify loop fails toward honesty: exit 1 now strictly means the mutation was never sent; every post-send bridge rejection is exit 2 with the rejection code in the JSON (a handler that failed mid-edit can leave a partial change inside one closed undo block, so "nothing changed" cannot be promised from outside); tune_param can no longer crash past an applied set without restore and disclosure; malformed bridge replies return structured errors instead of tracebacks; non-finite values are refused at the edges.

version.author: Dead Pixel Design
version.changelog: Closed-loop verify release. The bridge script itself is unchanged — the verify loop is a client-side sequencer of existing bridge commands — but the version moves in lockstep with the repo release, which adds: `reaperd.py measure` (one preflight-gated capture with measured metrics: LUFS-I always, spectrum/peak/RMS/stereo with Post Mortem installed); `reaperd.py verify` (capture -> run one mutating command -> capture the same frozen window again on the GUID-pinned track -> measured deltas, with an honest 0 VERIFIED / 1 not-applied / 2 UNVERIFIED exit-code contract); and the MCP tools verify_change and tune_param (iterative parameter search against a measured audio target, hard-capped at 5 renders, honest converged/unconverged/non-monotone reporting). Requires the agent-side files from the repo clone — ReaPack alone does not deliver them.

version.author: Dead Pixel Design
version.changelog: First-run render-statistics modal fix for Post Mortem. Captures temporarily enable REAPER 7.75+'s retain-render-statistics preference together with render-window auto-close, read the statistics, then restore the user's exact setting. This prevents the synchronous bridge from hanging behind the new Yes/No prompt.

version.author: Dead Pixel Design
version.changelog: Fresh-heartbeat authority fix for packaged macOS clients. A current bridge heartbeat now wins over a false-negative best-effort REAPER process probe, while missing or stale heartbeats still fail closed. Includes 3.11.1. Managed startup watchdog fix for Post Mortem P3-006. setup/install.py now installs the watchdog instead of a one-shot loader, reads both the current JSON bridge lock and legacy bare-epoch locks, waits 60 seconds before reclaiming a normal stale lock, preserves a render lock for up to six hours, and never blindly deletes a live lock. Includes 3.11.0. Panel support commands (Post Mortem Phase 3, P3-002). Two new read-only commands: get_selected_track reports the first selected track (identity, fx_count, item_count, receive_count) plus what a capture would do right now — capture_source (active time selection vs edit cursor, the same resolution capture_track_audio uses), capture_start_seconds, items_at_capture_start, and expected_capture_scope (isolated_track | full_mix | master_output). get_selected_track replaces the pre-3.11 undocumented minimal reply (top-level name/guid kept for compatibility; no-selection returns selected=false instead of erroring). get_capture_preflight reports everything that would gate or degrade a capture WITHOUT rendering: the allow_risk_level_3 gate (typed capture_gated blocker; the flag is read once at REAPER startup), SWS presence, render auto-close state (render_hang_risk warning when auto-close can be neither observed on nor forced), and optionally a target track's expected capture provenance. Additive only; no existing command changed. Includes 3.10.0. Preview lifecycle (Post Mortem Verified Fix Preview, P2-002). Three new commands: preview_change snapshots first, persists preview state to disk, then applies one temporary change (track volume dB, pan, FX normalized param, FX bypass) with every supplied identity field re-verified live — any mismatch refuses with STALE_IDENTITY and mutates nothing; one active preview at a time. cancel_preview restores the full snapshot. commit_preview re-verifies identities, restores the baseline value, then re-applies the proposed value inside EXACTLY ONE named undo point; nothing else in the lifecycle touches undo history. Crash/restart recovery: a leftover preview restores automatically at startup (cancel semantics) and is surfaced in the heartbeat; previews expire after 30 minutes via the defer loop. dry_run honored inside all three (they bypass the run_command dry_run gate by design). Includes 3.9.0. Track state snapshot/restore (Post Mortem Verified Fix Preview, P2-001). Two new commands: snapshot_track_state writes a crash-safe state file BEFORE any mutation covering exactly what preview operations can change (track volume, pan, per-FX enabled state with GUID identity, named FX parameter normalized values; a parameters[] entry that doesn't resolve fails the whole snapshot closed). restore_track_state resolves the track by GUID only (deleted track fails closed, nothing written), matches FX by GUID against the live chain so a moved FX still restores at its live index, restores everything that resolves, and reports what it could not in unrestored[] with typed reasons. Restore never touches state the snapshot does not contain. Additive only; no existing command changed. Includes 3.8.3. capture_track_audio regression fix: 3.8.2's solo-based isolation silenced captures of tracks that have media items (e.g. guitar tracks whose amp-sim FX do not render when the track is isolated offline). Solo isolation is now applied ONLY to item-less routing tracks (Kontakt multi-out stems etc.), which it isolates correctly; tracks with media items fall back to the plain selected-track render instead of returning silence. IMPORTANT/known limitation: for item-based tracks that plain render returns the full master mix, not the isolated track, so single-track measurements on such tracks reflect the whole mix; the capture reply's note now says so explicitly. Item-less routing-track isolation also bypasses every downstream bus FX (parent folders + master) so the capture is the track's own signal only. True per-track isolation for item-based tracks (amp-sim offline-render problem) remains open. Includes 3.8.2. capture_track_audio isolation fix: captures of item-less routing tracks (e.g. Kontakt multi-out drum stems) were returning the full mix, not the named track. REAPER's "stems (selected tracks)" render only renders tracks that hold media items; an item-less track silently fell back to the master mix, so every stem came back identical. The capture now exclusive-solos the target track for the render (restoring every track's solo state afterward) so any track isolates correctly. Same change bypasses the master-bus FX chain for the render, so the mastering chain no longer colors per-track measurements (LUFS/peak/spectrum); master-FX state is restored afterward. This fixes Post Mortem's cross-track masking, which was comparing the mix against itself. Includes 3.8.1. Render-dialog-hang fix: a capture_track_audio or render no longer hangs the bridge on a fresh install. REAPER's render-progress window blocks the synchronous render until dismissed unless its "Automatically close when finished" checkbox is ticked; the bridge now forces that setting (renderclosewhendone bit 0) on for the render and restores the user's prior value afterward, via SWS. Without SWS it degrades gracefully and the reply carries render_autoclose_warning instead of risking the hang. Includes 3.8.0. Bridge robustness (Phase 4 of the 2026-07-02 review): a crash mid-render no longer bricks the bridge (render locks reclaim after 6h); command ids are sanitized before naming the outbox reply (path traversal + non-string crash closed); the singleton lock writes atomically; heartbeats now actually carry the in-flight-command marker so a long sampler load reads as busy, not dead; json decoder refuses null array elements (they silently shifted later elements) and lone low surrogates. Includes 3.6.0. Platform correctness (Phase 3 of the 2026-07-02 review): Windows error replies carry the real UPPER_SNAKE code (the drive letter in the script path used to decode every error as code "C"); Linux status/jam no longer report DEAD when pgrep misses the lowercase reaper binary (both names matched, and a miss defers to the heartbeat). Includes 3.5.0. Broken-features cluster (Phase 2 of the 2026-07-02 review): discover-map actually reads .midnam note names (GetTrackMIDINoteNameEx; the old call could never return a name); short drum lanes really loop (longer-than-section and non-dividing lanes tile correctly instead of rendering silence); riff accepts 24-bit PCM (REAPER's default record format) and WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE; eq/setparam scan every FX parameter via paginated limit/offset (max_params was silently ignored, hiding EQ bands past index 200). Includes 3.4.0 (honesty cluster: requeue triage, stale-reply clear, evidence-gated eq/setparam/send exits).
